gen_risks.description: Weak strategic planning and policy implementation deficits across state administration could impair project execution and cross-ministerial reform coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an inter-ministerial Policy Planning, Monitoring, and Coordination Working Group led by the Public Policy Secretariat to oversee performance targets and coordinate reforms.
gen_risks.evidence: Section I.A, Paragraph 3: 'recognizing that weak planning and implementation deficits are among the most significant risks to the reform program.'

gen_risks.description: Lack of World Bank fiduciary and procurement experience in implementing agencies (PPS, MoE, MoLEVSA) may cause project delays and procurement non-compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified procurement and financial management specialists into PPS and MoLEVSA prior to implementation and provide intensive Bank procurement training.
gen_risks.evidence: Section VI.D, Paragraph 86: 'most of the entities involved in project implementation, have no experience in implementing World Bank-funded projects and with Bank procurement'

gen_risks.description: Complex clearance procedures between the Public Policy Secretariat and line ministries could delay procurement evaluations and contract approvals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear timeline agreements for evaluation clearances between PPS and line ministries, and implement close Bank monitoring of procurement schedules.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 4, Table 32: 'arrangements for clearance of evaluation reports by the PPS may lead to procurement delays due to consultation with the respective implementing institutions'

gen_risks.description: Overlapping mandates and non-transparent operating structures among Ministry of Economy development agencies (SIEPA, Development Fund, AOFI, NARR) could hinder investment and export promotion reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formulate and officially adopt an overarching strategic framework and action plan to restructure MoE agencies, consolidate support functions, and introduce systematic M&E.
gen_risks.evidence: Section III.A, Paragraph 29: 'The system of support provided by the MoE's agencies is complex and non-transparent... agencies have overlapping mandates, little coordination'

gen_risks.description: High tax wedges on low wages combined with social benefit withdrawal rules create strong work disincentives, trapping social assistance beneficiaries in formal unemployment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design and pilot an in-work cash transfer program for social financial assistance recipients to offset benefit reductions and lower effective marginal tax rates upon formal employment.
gen_risks.evidence: Section III.A, Paragraph 51: 'Serbia has one of the highest tax wedges on low-paying jobs... and a social assistance benefit that is reduced by at least one dinar'

gen_risks.description: Severe dispersion and high average caseloads per case worker across NES branch offices prevent effective individual client case management and job matching.
gen_risks.mitigation: Introduce a special registry for temporarily inactive jobseekers, reassign administrative staff to case management, and implement a standardized case worker certification system.
gen_risks.evidence: Section III.A, Paragraph 46: 'the average caseload varies between around 200 to over 2,000 registered unemployed per case worker across branch offices'

gen_risks.description: Low and fluctuating budgetary expenditure on Active Labor Market Programs (ALMPs) risks curtailing effective employment assistance to jobseekers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Condition results-based loan disbursements on maintaining ALMP allocations and deploy statistical profiling to target scarce resources to high-risk jobseekers.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3, Paragraph 25: 'ALMPs represented only 0.05 percent of GDP in 2013... low relative to other Eastern European countries'

gen_risks.description: Grant-financed enterprise innovation subprojects supported by the Innovation Fund could cause localized physical environmental impacts during product prototyping or testing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Subject all sub-grant applications to Environmental and Social Management Framework screening and mandate site-specific Environmental Management Plans for Category B subprojects.
gen_risks.evidence: Section VI.F, Paragraph 90: 'Direct, physical environmental impacts could arise under Component 2 on Innovation... Mini & Matching Grant Programs... development of new or significantly improved technologies'

gen_risks.description: Academic incentives favoring scientific publications over commercialization and lack of tech transfer mechanisms impede market application of public research.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a centralized Technology Transfer Facility at the Innovation Fund and introduce performance-based financing criteria for public research institutes.
gen_risks.evidence: Section III.A, Paragraph 41: 'very strong academic culture... with little incentives for protection of intellectual property or its commercialization... public research sector suffers from being disconnected'

gen_risks.description: Insufficient initial funding allocated to the Technology Transfer Facility may restrict the volume and demonstration impact of technology transfer transactions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require minimum state budget allocations of EUR 0.9 million annually for the TTF in 2017–2018 under DLI 4 and prepare proposals for donor scaling-up.
gen_risks.evidence: Section III.A, Paragraph 41: 'Current TTF funding under SRITPP (i.e. EUR 1.18 mn) is deemed insufficient to finance and demonstrate a strong tech transfer pipeline'

gen_risks.description: Failure to achieve Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) within specified calendar semesters would cause delays or reductions in results-based loan disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize targeted technical assistance under Part B to support DLI execution, monitor progress semi-annually, and utilize partial payment mechanisms where permitted.
gen_risks.evidence: Section III.B, Paragraph 58: 'In the event a DLI is not achieved, a request for reassessment may be submitted... Part A reimburses EEPs conditioned on achievement of DLIs.'

gen_risks.description: Political economy resistance and leadership turnover within public research institutes could stall structural legislative and financing reforms in the public R&D sector.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct rigorous independent international audits and RDI self-assessments to build consensus around evidence-based reform scenarios prior to legislative submission.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3, Paragraph 17: 'comprehensive national reforms have been sporadic... largely due to political economy considerations, including severe resources constraints and intermittent leadership'

gen_risks.description: Low baseline private sector spending on research and development limits commercial demand for joint innovation projects and technology licensing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide matching grant co-financing to innovative private firms to lower financial and technological risk associated with early-stage commercial R&D investments.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3, Paragraph 14: '0.24 percent of GDP on business R&D expenditures is much lower than the EU average of 1.3 percent.'

gen_risks.description: Insufficient employer outreach and declining vacancy registrations at the National Employment Service constrain formal job matching performance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt an NES employer outreach action plan, set annual targets for direct employer visits, and monitor vacancy collection KPIs.
gen_risks.evidence: Section III.A, Paragraph 46: 'Currently, only a small share of job matches... are carried out by the NES... number of vacancies in the NES registry remains largely insufficient'

gen_risks.description: Policy advice or regulatory reform proposals developed under technical assistance activities could generate unexpected indirect environmental or social risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage an Independent Environmental and Social Expert to systematically screen all Technical Assistance terms of reference and outputs against World Bank safeguard policies.
gen_risks.evidence: Section VI.F, Paragraph 91: 'Possible indirect environmental and social impacts may result from TA provided under the Project, particularly related to reforms in Components 1 and 2'

gt_risks.description: Program success relies on continuous, engaged commitment from the Prime Minister, Deputy PM, Minister of Finance, Minister of Education/Science/Technological Development, Minister of Labor/Employment/Veterans/Social Affairs, and the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS); line ministries must sustain interest in policy coordination or the loan will not disburse. Risk is heightened by political instability, frequent historical changes in ministers/senior staff, and excessive concentration of decision-making at the top (per the Bank's Systematic Country Diagnostic).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strong communications with the public, private sector, civil society, and EU Delegation to maintain a broad-based reform coalition; Bank coordinates communications with the PM's office; periodic PPMC Working Group consultations with private sector/civil society; ongoing close consultation with the EU Delegation in Serbia.

gt_risks.description: Significant downside macroeconomic risks: lower-than-expected Eurozone recovery could hurt Serbia's exports, remittances, and capital flows (EU countries are its largest trading partners). Materializing fiscal risks (e.g. SOE subsidy reduction difficulties) or weakening growth/currency would require even greater fiscal consolidation in 2015-2016 to keep public debt sustainable; reduced exports/FDI or greater consolidation could dampen anticipated reform impact.
gt_risks.mitigation: Bank works closely with government and the IMF to keep SOE/public-utility reform on track and ensure it generates required fiscal savings.

gt_risks.description: Project works across three ministries (MoE plus development agencies, MoESTD, MoLEVSA) plus the PPS, creating implementation complexity for both government and Bank. Achieving the DLIs requires substantial external technical assistance, but Bank supervision resources are limited and the government is reluctant to borrow for TA (would rather minimize loan-funded TA or substitute other donor resources), risking inadequate TA resourcing.
gt_risks.mitigation: Team seeks complementary resources (e.g. CIIP Trust Fund) and leverages work from other WBG projects; collaborates with other donors such as the EU and USAID.

gt_risks.description: Overall coordination sits with the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS), created only in spring 2014 under the new government; as a new institution it lacks capacity and a full set of official administrative procedures for cross-ministry policy coordination. Substantial risk to both project implementation (fiduciary/safeguards requirements, cross-ministry results reporting) and coordination of the inter-ministerial PPMC Working Group.
gt_risks.mitigation: PPS expected to hire additional personnel for fiduciary requirements and project coordination; Bank provides TA through the CIIP trust fund to strengthen PPS capacity.

gt_risks.description: PPS currently has no fiduciary experience managing Bank projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Build capacity by establishing a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within the PPS responsible for implementation, adequately staffing its fiduciary functions.

gt_risks.description: Reforms create both winners and losers, and losers are often more visible and organized at the time of reform (e.g. beneficiaries of MoE incentives/subsidies, National Employment Service case-workers, researchers at research institutes slated for restructuring).
gt_risks.mitigation: Government to clearly communicate reform objectives, expected outcomes, and benefits throughout the process.
